newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh opposition demands poll chief's removal.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh opposition demands poll chief's removal.

text.p: Bangladesh opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia has accused Chief Election Commissioner Abu Hena of bias toward the ruling party and demanded his removal, newspapers reported on Saturday.
"He has not only failed to hold free and fair polls but he is also partisan," the Independent quoted former prime minister Khaleda as telling her supporters on Friday.
Khaleda, who heads the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), said Hena should be replaced by a Supreme Court judge to ensure fairness in future polls.
A parliamentary by-election and local council polls are to be held shortly, although dates have not been fixed.
Khaleda has been pressing for Hena's removal ever since the BNP lost to Hasina's Awami League in elections last June.
She alleged Hena had "helped the Awami League to win the elections" and she vowed not to participate in future polls unless he is dismissed.
Hena has rejected the BNP's charge as baseless.
The 1996 elections were widely acclaimed as free and impartial by local and foreign monitors.
Last week Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina urged opposition parties to participate in future by-elections.
The by-election in the district of Manikganj north of Dhaka is aimed at filling a vacancy in the 330-member parliament, caused by the death of a BNP legislator.
The BNP and its ally the Jamaat-e-Islami party recently boycotted parliamentary by-elections in eastern Habiganj and northern Thakugaon districts.
